headline: Goldman Sachs Report warns of AI Job Apocalypse
summary: A new report from Goldman Sachs explores the potential for AI to displace millions of jobs globally, sparking concerns about widespread economic disruption.
details: A recent report by Goldman Sachs delves into the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on the global workforce. It suggests that AI could automate a significant portion of current jobs, leading to widespread displacement across various sectors.

The investment bank's analysis estimates that up to 300 million full-time jobs worldwide could be affected by AI. This includes both white-collar and blue-collar roles, with administrative and legal professions particularly vulnerable.

While the report highlights potential job losses, it also acknowledges the creation of new jobs and increased productivity. However, it stresses the need for significant reskilling and adaptation to mitigate the economic shock.

The findings contribute to an ongoing debate among economists and technologists about AI's long-term societal effects. Policymakers are urged to consider strategies for workforce transition and support in the face of these technological shifts.

Goldman Sachs just dropped a bombshell report on AI's impact on jobs. It warns of an 'apocalypse' for 300 million workers globally.

While the report highlights potential job losses, it also acknowledges the creation of new jobs and increased productivity. However, it stresses the need for significant reskilling and adaptation to mitigate the economic shock.

The findings contribute to an ongoing debate among economists and technologists about AI's long-term societal effects. Policymakers are urged to consider strategies for workforce transition and support in the face of these technological shifts.

headline_marked: [[Cloudflare to block AI web crawlers]] by default, rebalancing content use for websites
headline: Cloudflare to block AI web crawlers by default, rebalancing content use for websites
summary: Cloudflare is implementing new default settings to prevent mixed-use crawlers from scraping sites for AI training, aiming to give website owners more control and commercial opportunities.
details: Cloudflare has announced plans to automatically block mixed-use web crawlers that simultaneously index for search engines and act as AI agents or trainers. This new default stance is more defensive, building on previous optional controls for customers.

Cloudflare's CEO, Matthew Prince, stated that with non-human traffic now dominating the internet, faster action is needed for a sustainable ecosystem. The company hopes these changes encourage mixed-use crawlers to separate search from AI agent use and training.

The rise of AI models visiting sites to pull up-to-date information has disrupted the traditional web traffic system, where visits indicated ad views or subscriptions. Cloudflare's initiative aims to rebalance the relationship between AI companies and website owners.

Starting September 15, 2026, new Cloudflare customers and new websites from existing subscribers will default to allowing search but blocking AI training and agent use on pages with ads. Mixed-use crawlers not offering this choice will also be blocked by default on ad-supported pages.

Free account users will also switch to these defaults unless they opt-out before the September 15 deadline. Cloudflare is also re-launching its "Pay Per Crawl" feature as "Pay Per Use," where site owners are paid when their content appears in AI chatbot answers, rather than just for crawling.

The move also indirectly targets Google, whose Googlebot acts as both a search indexer and an AI trainer for Gemini and AI Overviews. Cloudflare highlights that Google makes it difficult for publishers to be discoverable without also being used for AI training, pushing for clearer separation of crawler intent.
